chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: Whoever performs the funeral prayer over a woman should not stand at her middle; rather, he should be at the area near her chest. And when he performs the prayer over a man, then he should stand at his middle.

So this does not conflict with the first report, because the meaning of his saying, 'at the area near her chest,' is when he is close to the head. It may be expressed as being near the chest due to its closeness to it, and that is also further confirmed.

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the male deceased over whom the funeral prayer is performed
key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the earlier hadith report being reconciled with this one
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the female deceased over whom the funeral prayer is performed
key_terms.صَدْرَهَا: her chest area, meaning the upper part of the body near which one stands
key_terms.وَسَطِهِ: his middle, the position where one stands for the male deceased

ai.seo_question: Where should one stand when performing funeral prayer over a man or a woman in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the proper place where the person leading salat over a جنازة should stand in relation to the deceased. For a woman, he stands nearer the upper body, while for a man he stands at the middle. The closing statement clarifies how this wording is reconciled with another report.
